newsitem.title: UK: BP sees refining margins still under pressure.
newsitem.headline: BP sees refining margins still under pressure.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc (BP) said on Tuesday that it expected its refining profit margins to continue under pressure because of recent capacity expansion, although there could be some volatility over the winter.
Refining and marketing operating profits on a replacement cost basis slipped to 151 million stg in the third quarter from 161 million a year earlier.

However, in the first nine months of the year they rose strongly to 516 million stg from 337 million. BP said marketing margins were affected by a price lag with rising oil prices during the third quarter.

Chemicals showed some recovery from a weak second quarter, which was affected by maintenance shutdowns. However net operating profit of 130 million stg was sharply below the 225 million stg posted in the third quarter of 1995.

BP predicted "continuing demand strength" for polymers in the fourth quarter, particularly in the Far East. But it added that the benefit from this is likely to be offset by higher naphtha feedstock costs and an easing in demand for acetic acid and related products.
